one_line: Kakatiya general and dance theorist, author of the Nrtta Ratnavali in the 13th‑century Telugu country.

appearance.face: oval face, medium brown Telugu complexion, straight nose, sharp jawline, neatly trimmed moustache, calm observant eyes with a focused, thoughtful default expression
appearance.hair: rich black hair, medium length, parted at center and combed back into a small low knot; front kept smooth; wears a simple gold circlet band across the forehead, narrow and undecorated
appearance.costume: era‑accurate Kakatiya military‑court attire: a fitted long‑sleeve tunic (angiya) in deep maroon cotton with fine gold piping at cuffs and collar, worn under a sleeveless pale gold quilted cotton brigandine that reaches mid‑thigh; a broad woven sash in dark forest green tied at the waist with the knot slightly to the left, its ends hanging to the knee; below, straight‑cut cream‑coloured cotton trousers gathered at the ankle; on the forearms, brown leather bracers; simple brown leather sandals; jewellery kept modest—small gold stud earrings, a single thin gold chain around the neck, and a plain gold ring on his right hand.
appearance.signature: a medium‑length straight double‑edged sword with a slightly flared South Indian hilt and round pommel, sheathed in a dark brown scabbard hanging from his green waist sash, plus a rolled palm‑leaf manuscript tube tucked at his back to echo his Nrtta Ratnavali

ref_desc: Jayapa Senani is a medium‑brown, sharp‑jawed Kakatiya officer with a small topknot, gold forehead band, maroon tunic under pale‑gold brigandine, green waist sash, cream trousers, brown bracers and sandals, carrying a sheathed Deccan sword and a palm‑leaf manuscript tube.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of Jayapa Senani, the 13th‑century Kakatiya general and dance theorist: an athletic Telugu man in his late thirties with an oval, medium‑brown face, sharp jaw, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache and calm, focused eyes. His rich black hair is parted at the center, smoothed back into a small low knot, and encircled by a narrow gold band on his forehead. He wears a deep maroon long‑sleeve tunic with fine gold piping at the collar and cuffs beneath a sleeveless pale‑gold quilted brigandine that reaches mid‑thigh. A broad forest‑green woven sash wraps his waist, knotted slightly to the left with the ends hanging toward his knee, over straight cream‑coloured cotton trousers gathered at the ankle. Brown leather bracers cover his forearms, and simple brown leather sandals are on his feet. Keep jewellery modest: small gold stud earrings, a thin gold neck chain, and a plain gold ring. His signature sword—a medium‑length straight double‑edged blade with a subtly flared South Indian hilt and round pommel—rests in a dark brown scabbard hanging from his green sash on his left, while a rolled palm‑leaf manuscript tube sits tucked at his back, hinting at his Nrtta Ratnavali. Use a palette of deep maroon, pale gold, forest green, cream and brown, and show him front, side and back to clarify hair, garments, and gear.
